scenes.subtitle: The square in front of Notre-Dame

scenes.title: Today's view dissolves into the past

scenes.caption: Photo 1880
scenes.text: The chronicler Jean de Saint-Victor recorded in the Memorial Historiarum that the construction of Notre-Dame began between 24 March and 25 April 1163 with the laying of the cornerstone in the presence of King Louis VII and Pope…

scenes.caption: Photo 1880
scenes.text: After the French Revolution in 1789, Notre-Dame and the rest of the church's property in France were seized and made public property.

scenes.caption: Photo 1880
scenes.text: In 1805, Pope Pius VII awarded it honorary status as a minor basilica.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890
scenes.text: The 1831 publication of Victor Hugo's novel Notre-Dame de Paris (English title: The Hunchback of Notre-Dame) inspired interest which led to restoration between 1844 and 1864, supervised by Eugène Viollet-le-Duc.

scenes.caption: Photo 1900
scenes.text: In the 19th century, the cathedral hosted the coronation of Napoleon and the funerals of many of the French Republic's presidents.

scenes.caption: Photo 1900
scenes.text: Since 1905, Notre-Dame, like the other cathedrals in France, has been owned by the French government, with the exclusive rights of use granted to the French Roman Catholic Church.

scenes.caption: Photo 1900
scenes.text: Beginning in 1963, the cathedral's façade was cleaned of soot and grime.

scenes.caption: Photo 1900
scenes.text: A fire in April 2019 caused serious damage, closing the cathedral for extensive and costly repairs; it reopened in December 2024.

scenes.caption: Photo 1908
scenes.text: In the early 21st century, about 12 million people visited Notre-Dame annually, making it the most visited monument in Paris.

scenes.title: The place
scenes.text: Haussmann enlarged the square in the 1860s, wiping out the medieval lanes of the Île de la Cité. The cathedral was restored after the 2019 fire.
